neighbours.label: The preposition or word placing a person's hands, arms, fists, fingers or elbows ('punched his fists in', 'threw her hands in', 'her hands were on', 'elbows on'); the same prepositions with objects or feet, and hands doing something else, stay quiet.
fire: He raised his fists in triumph and shouted.
She held her hands behind her back.
He sat with his chin in his hands and his elbows on the table.
His hands were on his hips.
Rest your hand on the railing.
With her hand on his shoulder, she spoke.
Fingers on my chin, tilting my face up.
The crowd threw their arms in the air.
quiet: He washed his hands with soap and shouted.
She held her keys behind the desk.
He sat with his cup in the sink and his coat on the table.
His feet were on the mat.
Rest your bag on the railing.
With her bag on the shelf, she spoke.
Stamps on my letter, ready for the post.
The crowd threw their hats in the air.

short: word placing hands or arms on the body or in space
notes: Probes: 0.42-0.99; objects 0.00-0.09. The model cannot see ahead, so the reading comes from the body part before the preposition. The output direction suppresses ' grasp', ' hands', ' fingers' on this + pole.
